1	import {
2	  currentEntitlements,
3	  regeneratesUsedToday,
4	  recordGeneration,
5	  checkGeneration,
6	  type GenerationKind,
7	} from "@/lib/billing/entitlements";
8	import { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
9	
10	// Re-exported so the generator's call sites keep importing their gate and its
11	// error from one place. The class itself lives in `lib/billing/errors`, which
12	// carries no `server-only` — tests and any future client-side display of the
13	// remaining allowance must be able to reference it.
14	export { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
15	
16	/**
17	 * What the GATE needs to know.
18	 *
19	 * `occasion` is optional because only a regenerate is counted, and only per
20	 * occasion. A styled look is a flat capability check, and the styled action
21	 * resolves its occasion only after this gate — deliberately, so a free user is
22	 * turned away before paying for a forecast fetch.
23	 */
24	export type GenerationCheckRequest = {
25	  kind: GenerationKind;
26	  /** Required for `regenerate`; the allowance is per occasion. */
27	  occasion?: string;
28	  /** The user's LOCAL date — never the server's. */
29	  today: string;
30	};
31	
32	/** What the LEDGER needs. `generation_events.occasion` is NOT NULL. */
33	export type GenerationRequest = GenerationCheckRequest & { occasion: string };
34	
35	/**
36	 * The single gate every real generation passes through.
37	 *
38	 * It was written as a deliberate no-op so that adding a paid tier later would be
39	 * a change to THIS file rather than surgery across the generate action. This is
40	 * that change: the decision now lives in `lib/billing`, and this stays the one
41	 * call site the generator knows about.
42	 *
43	 * The three kinds are metered differently (docs/MONETISATION.md §2):
44	 *   drop       — always free, on every tier. The daily drop is never rationed.
45	 *   regenerate — free gets one per occasion per day.
46	 *   styled     — Pro only.
47	 */
48	export async function assertCanGenerate(
49	  _userId: string,
50	  req: GenerationCheckRequest,
51	): Promise<void> {
52	  const e = await currentEntitlements();
53	
54	  // Only a regenerate needs the counter, and it is per-occasion — so drops and
55	  // styled looks skip the query entirely rather than paying for an answer that
56	  // cannot change the outcome.
57	  const regeneratesUsed =
58	    req.kind === "regenerate" && req.occasion
59	      ? await regeneratesUsedToday(req.occasion, req.today)
60	      : 0;
61	
62	  const check = checkGeneration(e, { kind: req.kind, regeneratesUsed });
63	  if (!check.allowed) throw new QuotaExceededError(check.reason);
64	}
65	
66	/**
67	 * Record a generation that actually happened.
68	 *
69	 * Deliberately separate from the check, and called only AFTER the model request
70	 * succeeds: a failed generation costs the user nothing, so charging for one
71	 * would be charging for our own error.
72	 */
73	export async function noteGeneration(userId: string, req: GenerationRequest): Promise<void> {
74	  await recordGeneration(userId, req.occasion, req.today, req.kind);
75	}

1	-- Which tier a user is on. A plain text column with a check constraint rather
2	-- than an enum type: adding a tier later ('trialing', when the trial model is
3	-- decided) is then an ALTER of the constraint, not a type migration with a
4	-- rewrite.
5	--
6	-- This is the ONLY source of tier truth. Nothing derives a tier from a Stripe
7	-- webhook payload at read time; billing's job will be to write this column.
8	alter table public.profiles
9	  add column if not exists tier text not null default 'free'
10	  check (tier in ('free', 'pro'));
11	
12	-- `profiles` carries a self-update RLS policy, so without this a user could run
13	-- `update profiles set tier = 'pro'` from the browser with the anon key and
14	-- grant themselves the paid tier. RLS decides WHICH ROWS you may touch; it does
15	-- not decide which COLUMNS, so the policy alone cannot express "you own this row
16	-- but not this field".
17	--
18	-- Reads are unaffected (the own-row select policy still applies), and the local
19	-- dev override is an env var (FITCHECK_FORCE_TIER), not this column, so nothing
20	-- in development depends on writing it. Billing will write it as service_role.
21	revoke update (tier) on public.profiles from authenticated;
22	
23	-- Every real AI generation, recorded.
24	--
25	-- The `outfits` rows CANNOT serve as this counter, for two independent reasons:
26	--
27	--   1. A regenerate REPLACES the day's rows for an occasion (saveDailyLooks is
28	--      delete-then-insert), so the act of regenerating erases its own evidence.
29	--      Counting rows afterwards cannot tell a first drop from a fifth.
30	--   2. saveDailyLooks writes one row per LOOK, three per generation, so a row
31	--      count reports 3 after a single drop.
32	--
33	-- This ledger is append-only and is the only thing the meter reads.
34	create table if not exists public.generation_events (
35	  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
36	  user_id      uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
37	  occasion     text not null,
38	  generated_on date not null,          -- the user's LOCAL date, as with outfits
39	  -- Three kinds, not a boolean. "Style an outfit with this" (PR #22) is neither
40	  -- the day's free drop for an occasion nor a regenerate of one: recording it as
41	  -- a drop would mark that occasion as already dropped, and recording it as a
42	  -- regenerate would make styling eat the regenerate allowance.
43	  kind         text not null check (kind in ('drop', 'regenerate', 'styled')),
44	  created_at   timestamptz not null default now()
45	);
46	
47	alter table public.generation_events enable row level security;
48	
49	create policy generation_events_own on public.generation_events
50	  for all
51	  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)
52	  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
53	
54	-- The meter's hot path: "what has this user spent on their local today?"
55	create index if not exists generation_events_user_day_idx
56	  on public.generation_events (user_id, generated_on);
57	
58	grant select, insert on public.generation_events to authenticated;

1	import type { UiOccasion } from "./types";
2	
3	export type Weather = { tempC: number; rain: boolean };
4	
5	// v2 UI occasions → formality bands (Decision D9, widened — see below).
6	//
7	// An occasion is CONTEXT, not a dress code. "Evening" covers both a casual date
8	// and a black-tie dinner; "Work" covers both a creative studio in sneakers and a
9	// boardroom. What separates them is the user's dress code, which onboarding
10	// already collects (profiles.formality_min/max) and personalBand() applies.
11	// Narrow per-occasion bands used to encode one assumed dress code for everyone,
12	// which left a smart-casual wardrobe unable to produce a Work or Evening outfit
13	// at all. Every band now includes 3 (smart casual) — a legitimate answer anywhere.
14	const BANDS: Record<UiOccasion, [number, number]> = {
15	  everyday: [1.5, 3],
16	  work: [2, 4.5],
17	  weekend: [1, 3.5],
18	  evening: [2.5, 5],
19	};
20	
21	export function occasionBand(o: UiOccasion): [number, number] {
22	  return BANDS[o];
23	}
24	
25	export type DressCodeRange = {
26	  formality_min?: number | null;
27	  formality_max?: number | null;
28	};
29	
30	/**
31	 * The occasion band narrowed to the dress codes the user picked in onboarding
32	 * (`profiles.formality_min/max`, derived from `dress_codes`).
33	 *
34	 * This is the answer the quiz already collects and the generator previously
35	 * ignored: someone who said "Smart casual" was still asked for 3.5–5 on Evening
36	 * and got nothing. Padded by ±0.5 so a single dress code isn't a knife-edge, and
37	 * falls back to the plain occasion band when there's no overlap at all (e.g. a
38	 * black-tie-only wardrobe asking for Everyday) — better a slightly-off outfit
39	 * than none.
40	 */
41	export function personalBand(
42	  o: UiOccasion,
43	  profile?: DressCodeRange | null,
44	): [number, number] {
45	  const [olo, ohi] = occasionBand(o);
46	  const min = profile?.formality_min;
47	  const max = profile?.formality_max;
48	  if (min == null || max == null) return [olo, ohi];
49	
50	  const lo = Math.max(olo, Math.max(1, min - 0.5));
51	  const hi = Math.min(ohi, Math.min(5, max + 0.5));
52	  return lo > hi ? [olo, ohi] : [lo, hi];
53	}
54	
55	/**
56	 * An explicit Refine formality (1..5) REPLACES the band with that level ±1.
57	 *
58	 * It replaces rather than intersects because Refine is an explicit instruction:
59	 * previously it was capped at the occasion's ceiling, so a smart-casual profile
60	 * could never ask for a black-tie outfit no matter what it selected.
61	 */
62	export function applyFormalityOverride(
63	  band: [number, number],
64	  f: number | null,
65	): [number, number] {
66	  if (f == null) return band;
67	  return [Math.max(1, f - 1), Math.min(5, f + 1)];
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Fabrics that are wrong in real heat NO MATTER HOW THEY ARE MADE.
72	 *
73	 * This is the measured replacement for the season tag's incidental thermal
74	 * protection: season used to be a hard filter, so a sweater tagged
75	 * {Autumn,Winter} could never reach a July outfit. Season is now a preference
76	 * (see ./season.ts), so the guard moved to the temperature we already fetch.
77	 *
78	 * The list is deliberately SHORT, and notably does not contain wool.
79	 * Whether a wool garment suits 30°C is decided by its weight and weave, not its
80	 * fibre: tropical, fresco and high-twist wools are summer suiting, and merino is
81	 * used *for* heat because it wicks and breathes. `items.material` is a bare
82	 * fibre name today, so a "wool" rule cannot tell a summer-weight trouser from a
83	 * melton coat — it would exclude exactly the smart-casual work wear this app is
84	 * built around. Everything left here is insulation or a coarse heavy weave,
85	 * where no construction makes it summer-appropriate.
86	 *
87	 * Wool, merino and cashmere are not unprotected: an off-season piece still takes
88	 * the `seasonFit` penalty in scoring, so it ranks below linen in July. Demoted
89	 * on evidence rather than eliminated on a guess — the same argument this module
90	 * makes about season itself.
91	 *
92	 * The real fix is data, not a longer list. `item-data-completeness` (queue #3)
93	 * adds an `items.texture` column — Flat / Fine knit / Chunky knit / Brushed /
94	 * Fleece-back — and constrains `material` to a vocabulary that separates "Wool"
95	 * from "Merino wool". `item-signals-in-generator` (queue #12) then feeds
96	 * material × texture into SCORING. Warmth belongs there, as a weighted signal,
97	 * not here as a veto.
98	 */
99	const HOT_MATERIALS = ["fleece", "shearling", "down", "quilted", "puffer", "tweed"];
100	
101	/** Strictly above 25: 24° is pleasant, 26° is hot. */
102	const HOT_C = 25;
103	
104	export function weatherRules(w: Weather) {
105	  return {
106	    needsOuterwear: w.tempC < 15,
107	    excludeMaterials: [
108	      ...(w.rain ? ["suede", "canvas"] : []),
109	      ...(w.tempC > HOT_C ? HOT_MATERIALS : []),
110	    ],
111	  };
112	}
